notes: Inbound from self-serve signup — CTO signed up & ran quick proof-of-concept against a small Zendesk dataset.
Primary ask: reliable ticket summarization + structured JSON for downstream routing (priority, intent, product).
Also wants tool calling: auto-apply labels, trigger internal webhooks to update SLA fields and escalate to L2 when needed.
Quoted from call: 'We need sub-200ms summary latency for agent-facing UI — but ok with 300-400ms for async batch jobs.'
Cost sensitivity: SMB — wants predictable per-ticket pricing, will start with hosted and move to Dedicated only if volume justifies it.
Security: must support SSO/SAML for admin console, retention controls, and basic audit logs. SOC2 compliance referenced in procurement notes.
Integration notes: currently prototypes with OpenAI embeddings + heuristics; exploring Redwood for lower token cost and structured output / tool calling support.
POC scope: 10k tickets/month, 2 parallel agent UI calls per second (peak). Typical mean ticket length ~400 tokens; want KV cache for repeated contexts.
Technical preference: hosted_api for quick onboarding, expect to use streaming responses for UI, and structured-output schemas (JSON) for downstream ingestion.
AE notes: Jordan Blake — championing quick start, introduced Maya Chen (SE) for a technical deep-dive. Legal loop expected mid-March.
Customer persona: small engineering team (3 backend, 2 frontend), product-led growth; they want a demo app showing tool-calls to label + create follow-up tasks.
Edge cases called out: noisy tickets (multi-thread), attachments (PDF), and non-English support (limited to en/fr for now).
Risk: budget TBD — CFO wants a one-month trial first; 'If it reduces agent time by >20% we can sign annual', per CTO.
Requested artifacts: sample webhook signature example, rate-limit guidance, simple pricing calc for 10k/mo tickets.
Friendly to Redwood: developer-first mindset, asked specifically about SDKs and quickstart examples in Node and Python.
